one_liner: Rust compiler cache for Unreal Engine that impersonates IncrediBuild's xgConsole to speed up re-compiles vs. no cache.
what_it_does: octobuild is a compiler cache for Unreal Engine and UE-based games, distributed as xgConsole/ib_console binaries that impersonate IncrediBuild's XGE console tools, which UBT/UAT already invoke when the XGE executor is enabled. On each compile action it caches the resulting object file on local disk (default 64GB, configurable) keyed off the compile inputs, falling back to the real cl.exe (MSVC) or clang compiler on a miss. No changes to game/engine build scripts are needed beyond enabling the XGE executor and, on Linux/macOS, applying the UE patches listed in the README.
how_it_is_fast: It is a content-addressed disk cache of individual compile actions, similar in spirit to ccache/sccache, avoiding re-invocation of cl.exe/clang for translation units it has already built. The repo also ships octo_agent/octo_builder/octo_coordinator and a src/cluster module, suggesting optional distributed-build support beyond local caching, but this is undocumented in the README and not covered by the benchmark. Per the README's own numbers the entire measured speedup is cache-hit driven: at 0% cache hit rate it is roughly neutral to slower than no octobuild at all, presumably from added hashing/IPC overhead.
when_to_use: Unreal Engine or UE-based game project doing iterative DebugGame rebuilds after small source edits, with a cache that can stay warm between builds
Team already using, or willing to enable, IncrediBuild-style XGE executor integration in UBT/UAT
Windows target with MSVC 2019/2022 (the benchmarked and best-documented path)
Linux or macOS target where you can apply the listed UE engine patches (some already merged in UE >= 5.2 / >= 5.3)
Dev or CI machines with spare local SSD space for a large (default 64GB) persistent cache
when_not_to_use: Cold-cache or from-scratch CI builds: the README's own table shows octobuild is equal to or up to ~25% slower than no octobuild at 0% cache hit rate (Win64 8m4s -> 10m6s)
You need a validated comparison against ccache, sccache, distcc, or IncrediBuild itself — none appears in the README; the only baseline is 'without octobuild'
Non-Unreal C/C++ projects: it's UE-specific (vs/clang compiler pre/postprocessing, XGE action-graph parser), not a general-purpose compiler cache
You can't spare disk for a multi-GB persistent cache, or your build environment is ephemeral so the cache never warms up
You need compiler flags and an exact reproducible harness for the benchmark numbers — the README doesn't state flags and uses an unnamed game project

integration.dependencies: Rust crates (bincode, crossbeam-channel, petgraph, reqwest, serde, sha2, xml-rs, figment, thiserror, uuid, etc.) plus the octobuild/daemon-rs and octobuild/ipc-rs git dependencies; winapi/winreg on Windows. Also distributed as prebuilt packages via Chocolatey, WinGet, Homebrew, and apt/deb.
integration.min_toolchain: Rust stable (edition 2021 crate, CI builds against dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable with no pinned MSRV); Windows build additionally needs Visual Studio 2019 or 2022 with the C++ desktop workload
integration.platforms: Win64 (MSVC 2019/2022), Linux, macOS, plus PS4/PS5/Xbox One/Xbox Series X and Android/iOS listed as supported; console/mobile targets build through UE's own toolchains
integration.thread_safety: not documented explicitly; uses a worker pool (src/worker.rs) with concurrency capped by the OCTOBUILD_PROCESS_LIMIT setting (default: core count)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — on Windows it plugs into UBT/UAT's existing XGE executor hook with no engine source changes; on Linux/macOS it additionally requires the UE engine patches listed in the README (some already merged into UE >= 5.2 / 5.3)

gotchas: Cold cache makes the build slower than not using octobuild at all (README: Win64 8m4s without octobuild vs. 10m6s at 0% cache hit)
Default disk cache is 64GB; tune via OCTOBUILD_CACHE_LIMIT_MB, and OCTOBUILD_CACHE_MODE can set it to read-only or fully disabled
On Windows, long command lines can hit 'ERROR: The filename or extension is too long (os error 206)' — fix is OCTOBUILD_USE_RESPONSE_FILES=true, which is already the Windows default
Source tree contains cluster/agent/coordinator/builder binaries implying distributed (multi-machine) build support, but this is undocumented in the README and unmeasured in the benchmark
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick octobuild specifically because the project is Unreal Engine or UE-based — its xgConsole/ib_console impersonation and MSVC/clang postprocessing are UE-specific integration points that NativeLink, FASTBuild, and HOMCC don't provide. Those siblings target generic CMake/Ninja or distcc-based C/C++ builds and would need a custom UE integration to be used at all, whereas octobuild works with UBT/UAT's existing XGE executor path out of the box.
verified_claims_summary: The README's first-party benchmark table (unnamed UE 5.0.3 game project, DebugGame configuration, no stated compiler flags) shows a fully warm (100%) cache beating a build without octobuild by about 2.4x-6.5x across platforms — e.g. Linux 3m54s to 36s, Win64 8m4s to 2m15s (MSVC 2019) — on an AMD Ryzen 7 3700X/32GB (Linux) or Intel Core i7-9700F/32GB (Windows/console) with SSD storage; a cold (0%) cache showed no speedup and was up to ~25% slower on Win64 (8m4s to 10m6s).
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-15, 285 stars, packaged for Chocolatey/WinGet/Homebrew/apt) and MIT-licensed, but it's a set of UE-specific CLI binaries rather than a general library, so 'copyable' means vendoring the tool, not embedding source into another project.
